plan.title: Made to Stick
plan.author: Chip Heath and Dan Heath
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's framework, chapter structure and main examples well, though I would avoid quoting exact figures or wording from memory.
plan.one_liner: Why do urban legends spread while good ideas fade? Six principles that make any message stick.
plan.summary: Why do some ideas grab us and refuse to let go, while others vanish the moment we hear them? Chip and Dan Heath argue that sticky ideas are not born lucky. They are built. Studying urban legends, proverbs, ad campaigns and classroom lessons, the brothers find six shared traits. Sticky ideas are simple, unexpected, concrete, credible, emotional, and told as stories. The first letters spell SUCCESs. The main enemy is the Curse of Knowledge. Once we know something, we can no longer imagine not knowing it, so we explain things in abstract, expert language that others cannot grasp. Through vivid examples from business, teaching, medicine and charity, the book shows how anyone can find the core of a message and craft it so people understand it, remember it, and act on it.
